column11: two figures multiplied. (1) Swaminathan S, Leung N, Lager DJ, Melton LJ 3rd, Bergstralh EJ, Rohlinger A, Fervenza FC, 'Changing incidence of glomerular disease in Olmsted County, Minnesota: a 30-year renal biopsy study', Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2006;1(3):483-487, doi 10.2215/CJN.00710805, PMID 17699249, is the only US population-based biopsy series with a defined denominator: for 1994 to 2003 it gives an annual incidence of membranous nephropathy of 1.0 per 100,000 a year, age and sex adjusted to the 2000 US population. Applied to the 341,784,857 US residents at 2025-07-01 (Census Vintage 2025, NC-EST2025-AGESEX-RES, both sexes, POPESTIMATE2025, www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2025/national/asrh/nc-est2025-agesex-res.csv): 3,417.84857 x 1.0 = 3,418 cases of membranous nephropathy a year. (2) 80% of membranous nephropathy is primary rather than secondary: Couser WG, 'Primary Membranous Nephropathy', Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017;12(6):983-997, doi 10.2215/CJN.11761116, PMID 28550082, states that 80% of cases are renal limited; Ronco P, Beck L, Debiec H et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2021;7(1):69, doi 10.1038/s41572-021-00303-z, state approximately 80% primary; a London biopsy cohort reads 81.8% (121 of 148, Gupta S et al., BMC Nephrol 2017;18:201, doi 10.1186/s12882-017-0615-5). 3,418 x 0.80 = 2,734 primary membranous nephropathy diagnoses a year
column12: Olmsted County is small, overwhelmingly white and twenty years old, and it counts only biopsied disease, so it misses patients never biopsied. It is used anyway because it is the one US rate with a published denominator. The widely quoted alternative, 12 per million a year rising to 20 per million if non-progressors are counted (Couser 2017), gives 4,101 to 6,836 cases of membranous nephropathy a year, so this row sits at the BOTTOM of the US band. A UK cohort of 381 cases reads 6.55 per million (Storrar J et al., Clin Kidney J 2024;17(4):sfae066, doi 10.1093/ckj/sfae066), below every US figure

column11: stated equal to the incidence above, which sets the engine's carryover to zero: each year's eligible pool is that year's primary membranous nephropathy diagnoses and the penetration is the share of them started on therapy. It is used here because no US prevalence of membranous nephropathy is published at all: the nearest openable figures are a UK Biobank cohort of 502,507 participants aged 40 to 70 with 72 per million at baseline (Hamilton P et al., PLoS One 2023;18(4):e0281795, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0281795), which on the US population would be 24,608 but is drawn from the disease's peak age band, and a paid market-research model that cannot be opened. column11: the measured share of US primary membranous nephropathy patients who actually receive a B-cell-directed therapy. Laurin L-P, Helmuth M, Almaani S et al., 'Risk Factors for Disease Progression for Adults and Children With Membranous Nephropathy in the Cure Glomerulonephropathy Network (CureGN)', Kidney Int Rep 2025;10(6):1917-1928, doi 10.1016/j.ekir.2025.03.027, PMID 40630289, follow 591 biopsy-confirmed primary membranous nephropathy patients enrolled 2010 to 2023 at US, Canadian, Polish and Italian sites and report that anti-B cell therapy was used in 44% of patients. 2,734 x 0.44 = 1,203 patients a year. This is used in place of a built-up eligibility filter because it already embeds the KDIGO risk stratification NCT07851220 screens on: the 2021 KDIGO glomerular diseases guideline reserves rituximab, cyclophosphamide with glucocorticoids, or a calcineurin inhibitor with rituximab for the moderate and high risk strata, which are defined by proteinuria above 3.5 g a day persisting after six months of renin-angiotensin blockade, the same threshold as the trial's urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 3.5 or more after at least three months of maximally tolerated therapy
column12: the number to argue with, and the alternatives bracket it rather than beat it. A natural-history construction gives less: about 20% of patients present with subnephrotic proteinuria and about a third of nephrotic patients remit spontaneously (Couser 2017; Polanco N et al., J Am Soc Nephrol 2010;21(4):697-704, doi 10.1681/ASN.2009080861, 104 of 328 conservatively treated patients, at 14.7 months), so 0.80 x 0.667 = 0.533 would be the untreated-eligible share and 0.44 sits below it, which is the right direction since not every eligible patient is treated. Pushing up, 73% of the CureGN cohort had active disease at enrolment. CureGN is a registry of biopsied patients at academic centres, so it over-represents the treated end of the disease, and it is not US-only

column11: a judgement, and the competitive case is unusually specific. Rituximab is the KDIGO 2021 first-line recommendation for membranous nephropathy at moderate or high risk of progression, it is available as a biosimilar at a small fraction of a new biologic's price, and it has randomised evidence behind it. Obinutuzumab, a second anti-CD20, is already in a Phase 3 in this disease (MAJESTY, NCT04629248) and has beaten rituximab in refractory series (75.0% against 35.5% response at 6 months, Obinutuzumab versus rituximab for refractory primary membranous nephropathy, Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025;40(5):978). NCT07851220 randomises inebilizumab against tacrolimus, not against rituximab, so even a clear win leaves the standard of care untested head to head and a payer with an obvious cheaper first step

column11: NCT07598825 requires either an inadequate response to at least 9 months of standard of care, defined as ALT at or above twice the upper limit of normal after prednisone above 5 mg a day plus a conventional steroid-sparing agent at full dose, or intolerance of standard of care within 6 months of screening. That is one share, and it is published as one: Ergenc I, Frolkis A, Chung Y, Heneghan MA, 'Evolution of Therapy in Autoimmune Hepatitis', Gastroenterology and Hepatology 2025;21(3), second-line treatment section: 'Approximately 20% of patients experience insufficient response or intolerance to first-line therapy, necessitating exploration of alternative treatment approaches'. 71,757 x 0.20 = 14,351 US adults
column12: the components, from the AASLD 2019 practice guidance (Mack CL, Adams D, Assis DN et al., Hepatology 2020;72(2):671-722, doi 10.1002/hep.31065): treatment failure 'occurs in 7%-9% of adults', incomplete response 'occurs in ~15% of adults and children', and 'treatment-ending side effects occur in 13%'. Those cannot simply be added, because the intolerant patients largely overlap the others and most are rescued by mycophenolate rather than needing a biologic, which is why the single 20% figure is used rather than a sum of 35%. The case for a larger pool: on the modern endpoint of insufficient biochemical response at six months the share is 24% in a US health system (Yao J et al., Hepatol Commun 2025;9(11):e0824) and 36% in a European validation cohort (Grossar L et al., JHEP Rep 2024;6(9):101149, doi 10.1016/j.jhepr.2024.101149), which would put the pool at 17,200 to 25,800. The case for a smaller one: the European guideline puts frank treatment failure at probably less than 5%. The range is definitional rather than empirical and 20% is the middle of it

column11: a judgement. Nothing is approved as second-line therapy in autoimmune hepatitis anywhere: mycophenolate and tacrolimus are used off label and cost very little, and the AASLD guidance reports mycophenolate biochemical response of 82% in azathioprine-intolerant patients, so a large part of the eligible pool is salvaged cheaply before any biologic is reached. Against that, the patients who genuinely fail rather than merely cannot tolerate first-line therapy respond to mycophenolate only about a third as often, and they are the ones with the worst outcomes: lack of a complete biochemical response within six months is the strongest independent predictor of liver-related death or transplant, hazard ratio 5.7 (95% CI 3.4 to 9.6) across 2,559 patients (Slooter CD et al., Hepatology 2024;79(3):538-550, doi 10.1097/HEP.0000000000000589). A first approved biologic takes the hard end of the pool rather than the whole of it
